findings.what: The framework's own per-frame record of the dense scroll reports build_ms p50 9, p95 781, max 1087, with 196 of 886 frames over 400 ms; I recomputed it from per_frame and every 300-frame window in the record holds between 64 and 69 of them, the longest run with no heavy frame is 6 frames, and the cost tracks paper rather than rows: median build is 3 ms on frames that draw no paper piece, 9 ms on one piece and 654 ms on two (n=187, max 1087), corr(build, pieces_drawn) 0.788 against corr(build, rows_built) -0.122 and corr(build, masks_composed) -0.003.
findings.why: "No scroll jank against the year-deep seeded history" is the row's own words, and the build's instrument says roughly every fourth frame of a throw costs two-thirds of a second of the app's own layout and paint; the file itself rules out the machine ("build_ms is the framework laying out and painting: the app's own work" against "raster_ms ... says what this machine costs", and raster is only p50 102 / max 225), and the clip cannot show it because its clock is driven at a fixed 16 ms a step (frames.json: step_ms 16, playback_over_app_time 1.0) so 11_chat_scroll.fling.json's "300 of 300 frames moved exactly what they were asked, frames_under_a_device_pixel 0" is a property of the driven clock, not of a phone.

findings.where: per_frame build_ms, against evidence/logs/scroll_webkit.json and what_the_alternates_cost.json's the_fling_alone
findings.what: The set carries its own control for the finding above and the capture is 23x worse than it. The same instrument, the same fling (travelled 27645 logical px in both, rows_built_total 170 against the capture's 167), the same driven clock and the same 360x780x3 viewport, run on 2026-09-11: build p50 5 ms, p95 34.3 ms, 6 of 628 frames over 400 ms and all six at frames 14-18, 45 and 211 — none in the last 300; the plain-fonts arm reads p95 33.7 and 5 of 627. what_the_alternates_cost.json states the_fling_alone.over_400_ms = 0 for both arms. This capture's record: p95 781 ms and 65 of its last 300 frames over 400 ms.
findings.why: The row asks whether the scroll is dependable against the year of history, and the only two prior measurements of the identical throw in the evidence say it was, two days before the capture; nothing in the evidence set says what changed, and the experiment's own README already names the mechanism that is still there ("sixty paper pieces rebuilt on every fourth frame, which is the positioned list re-anchoring and a LayoutBuilder on the hot path"). The two arms were built from a different commit than the capture, so this is a change over two days rather than a controlled A/B — but it is the same instrument on the same scene.

findings.where: problems and ok, with sync.last_fault in the matching .report.json
findings.what: Three of the fifteen captured scenes ended ok: false, each with problems = ["http: 401 GET http://127.0.0.1:8480/v1/events?after=<cursor>&wait=20", "console: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 401 (Unauthorized)"], and their reports carry sync.last_fault "401 the signature does not match" (11: 1 fault in 212 rounds; 14: 1 in 19; 15: 1 in 453). The other twelve scene logs are ok: true with empty problems.
findings.why: That request is the long poll that carries every incoming event from the other phone, and a signature the host will not accept is the failure mode in which messages simply stop arriving with nothing on the glass to say so. In all three the client recovered (cursor equals events at the end) but nothing in the evidence says why the signature stopped matching or that recovery is guaranteed, and 20 per cent of the captured scenes hitting it is not a one-off.

findings.where: view.reactions, and the top row of the still
findings.what: Reactions are named in the row and no reaction is legible in any artifact. Across every region report in the set, view.reactions is non-empty exactly once: 13_messenger_states.report.json, {"01M1MCJ1M0D46H1D74PPV4NMNH": 1}. That id is row 8071 (rows_cost: tall 93, top -59), so clipped_at_an_edge 0.366 is the fraction of it on the glass; measured on the PNG, the visible band runs y 282-306 device px and carries 5 pixels darker than luma 120 in 880 columns — 0.6 per cent ink, no mark of any kind. The same row is also in taken_back. evidence/scenes/13_messenger_states.json has no react step among its nine far lines (read, message, edit, reply, message, unsend, read, typing on, refuse), while evidence/scenes/02_chat.json's viewport note gives as its reason for not photographing one there that "13_messenger_states is where a reaction and a reply are photographed". The reply is there (replies_on_the_glass names the row it answers). The reaction is not.
findings.why: A capability the rubric enumerates, that the set's own plan says is photographed here, and that cannot be seen in a single frame or still. reliability.json's react check and spine_schema_test say the mechanism exists; the pictures say nobody photographed it.

findings.what: The reconnect happens between two frames and the message that came back is never readable. Frame 671 shows the banner "can't reach the other phone. it'll go when it can." and the note "on my way - leaving in ten / Thu 3 Sep 19:40 / waiting to send"; frame 672 already has the banner gone, "sent ✓" on that note, and both queued far rows in place. I measured 671->672 at a mean absolute luma change of 41.09 grey levels over 53.5 per cent of the pixels — twelve times the clip's own mean_change_per_frame of 3.41 — a single-frame cut, and frames.json's cuts_between_runs marks 671 as a run boundary: the harness stepped no frames across the 18,719 ms that 08_state_propagating.json's arrivals[-1].waited_ms records. Then, in all 24 frames of the final take, the far phone's message row (01M1MCJ1M079RT7T54CSV5QMJE, rows_cost row 8078, type message, listed in whole_on_the_glass) is a folded sheet carrying only the addressee "teo" and no words; 08_state_propagating.report.json's fold.playhead is 0 of the 142-frame unfold_thirds sequence at the end of the scene. The scene's far line for that moment is "message the bus is late, dont wait up", and neither of those phrases is on any frame.
findings.why: This clip is what the set offers in place of a headless log for "correct ordering after going offline and reconnecting". It does put the link going down and coming back on one screen, which is real — but the landing is a cut and the returning note never opens, so which message came back and where it sorted relative to the one the person wrote during the outage still has to be taken from a report field rather than read off the glass. The scene script calls unfold after the two earlier arrivals and does not call it after the reconnect, so this is a fault in how the picture was taken rather than in the app.

findings.where: transport, host.address, host.latency_ms, tailscale.checked_at and tailscale.later_check
findings.what: Every ordering and no-duplicate claim in the set was taken over loopback. reliability.json reads transport "local", host 127.0.0.1:42935, latency_ms 0, and on that basis reports 177 events each side, duplicates 0, same_order_both_sides true, ordering "monotonic", offline_queue "26 events queued offline, all delivered on reconnect" and reconnect_ordering "client holds seq 1..175 gapless and monotonic after the gap". Its tailscale block is dated checked_at 2026-09-05T00:28:43Z — eight days before this capture's 2026-09-13T09:37:45Z — and its later_check reads {"status": "pending", "why": "the nodes were not answering when this was re-run"}; coldstart.json is the same run and carries the same pending later_check.
findings.why: The row is about dropped, duplicated and reordered messages between two phones on a tailnet. A zero-latency loopback pair is the condition under which those faults are least likely to appear, and the one record of the same behaviour over an actual tailnet could not be reproduced on the day of the capture.

findings.what: First launch on a phone that already has the couple's year takes 7124 ms (01_pulse, store: fresh, of which "the log" is 4560 ms), 6675 ms (08, 4720 ms) and 6058 ms (dusk_pulse, 4077 ms). The other two fresh scenes are fast only because their store is empty: 10_first_run 2128 ms and 17_setup_pwa 1886 ms, with "the log" at 41 and 53 ms and events 0 in both reports. No artifact in the set pictures those six or seven seconds — there is no still or clip of the app between launch and first frame with the year in it, and the only statement about them anywhere in the evidence is a test name in evidence/logs/tests.log (the_first_ten_seconds_are_not_blank_test.dart: "nothing on it spins", "there is a surface, and it is the desk").
findings.why: "No spinner that outstays its welcome" is an item in the row, and it cannot be checked against any picture in the set; a six-to-seven-second wait every cold start is exactly long enough for it to matter, and what is on the screen for it does not exist as far as this evidence goes.

findings.what: At the end of the reconnect scene, with sync.link.state "connected", the report reads pending 1, cursor 14082 against events 14083, refused_in_the_outbox 0 and last_fault "offline (POST /events)" — one event written locally and never pushed, and the record does not name it. 13_messenger_states.report.json has the same pending 1 but accounts for it (refused_in_the_outbox 1, and the row on the glass says "it would not go"). The most likely candidate in 08 is a read marker for the rows that had just landed (view.folded_in.read_marker is 3), which would mean the other phone's "read" state is one event behind at the end of the scene.
findings.why: The row asks for delivery and read state that can be trusted. An outbox that is one event deep with the link up and nothing in the record saying which event it is means a reader cannot tell a lagging read marker from something the person wrote that has not gone.

findings.where: the transport bar under the film
findings.what: The elapsed counter is wrong for a short film. The still reads "0:00 / 0:03" with the scrub handle 26 per cent along its track, while 14_media_viewer.report.json says video.position_ms 649 of duration_ms 2500. All six panels of the strip read "0:00 / 0:03", across what 14_media_viewer.frames.json calls 48 frames at 33 ms = 1.58 s of app time, so the counter never ticks while the handle visibly moves. The same widget rounds 2500 ms up to 0:03 and 649 ms down to 0:00.
findings.why: The media viewer is a named capability; a position readout that says 0:00 for the whole of a film is a control that cannot be used to find a moment in it.

findings.where: the footer line of the rows carrying the marker
findings.what: The delivery and read markers are cut wherever they appear. 02_chat.report.json's delivery has exactly one entry — 0001DX0GAG1Z5VRR3JYSHYJQDF, state "read" — and clipped_at_an_edge gives it 0.742 on the glass (rows_cost row 7872: tall 94, top 725 against viewport_tall 794.7), which is why states_on_the_glass for that still is {}. On the PNG the footer "Tue 1 Sep 07:12 read ✓✓" is sliced horizontally through the middle of its glyphs by the composer's top edge. In 13_messenger_states.png the footer of "and the thing for the door" ("Thu 3 Sep 19:40 sent ✓", ink from y 1846 to about y 1890) runs into the sheet's own torn bottom fringe.
findings.why: Delivery and read state are in the row by name, and in the two stills where they appear they are the part of the picture that got cut.

findings.what: The hero chat still holds five notes, not eight. 02_chat.report.json: visible is 5 ids, whole_on_the_glass is 3, rows_cost is rows 7868-7872 (message, voice_note, photo, message, message) in a viewport_tall of 794.7; evidence/logs/tears.json counts the same still independently at visible 5, notes_with_tears 5, distinct_tears 5, repeats {}. The scene file's own justification for shooting the stills at 480 rather than 360 points is that "the brief asks for at least eight notes visible in 02_chat.png with no tear id repeated ... At 480 it holds eight, five of them on torn sheets, five distinct." The no-repeat half holds; the eight does not.
findings.why: Not this row's requirement, but it is the density of the thread and it is checkable: the reason given for the whole shooting decision is contradicted by two of this capture's own records.

findings.what: Nothing in the set shows a message on two screens, and nothing shows what an iPhone does with a push. MANIFEST.json.missing accounts for 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png with a measured reason rather than an excuse (no /dev/kvm, the x86_64 image under QEMU instruction emulation, adbd answering after 113 minutes with no framework behind it, no GTK for a desktop stand-in) but points at docs/PHONES.md, which is outside the evidence set and which I did not open. reception.json says browser "chromium", app_open false, and its own note says "this is not an iPhone banner, there is no lock screen in evidence, and what an installed iOS web app does with the same call is not shown anywhere in this build"; pwa.json says display_mode_standalone false, so the page was never read in the installed mode iOS requires for push at all.
findings.why: A messenger replacing Instagram DMs is judged on whether the other person's message reaches you when the app is shut. The records are honest about what they are not, and what they are not is the case that matters.

what_is_working: 13_messenger_states.png carries, on one screen and in the couple's own words, an edit ("and the bread — there is half a loaf in the tin / edited ✓ · sent ✓"), a withdrawal ("took this back"), a delivered reply quoting the row it answers, a refusal that says why ("it would not go ✗ / send it again / this phone is on an older version and cannot read that"), typing ("noor writing…"), four "sent ✓" and a composer holding both a draft and a reply chip; the report's refusals_on_the_glass and replies_on_the_glass carry the same text, and the reply's target event is given in full.

02_chat.png has a voice note with a waveform and 0:31, a photo with a caption, plain messages and a "read ✓✓" — four kinds of row in one viewport, with 04_moments.report.json reporting 183 media items (115 photo, 54 voice_note, 14 video), 52 tiles built and blobs asked 18 / arrived 18 / the_store_does_not_have 0 / tiles_without_a_picture 0.

12_search.png is a real search: the query on the glass, fifteen facet chips with "photographs" selected, the term highlighted in every hit, results newest-first (Wed 6 May, Thu 26 Mar, Sat 24 Jan), and 12_search.report.json reporting hits 6 with kinds {photo: 6} — the facet actually filters. reliability.json's search check answers nine queries across nine event types, each with the first hit of the wanted type.

08_state_propagating.mp4 does put a link going down and coming back on one screen and not in a settings string: the banner "can't reach the other phone. it'll go when it can.", a note that says "waiting to send", then the banner gone and "sent ✓", with the far phone's queued state landing as "— noor is quiet". 06_unfolding.mp4 shows a note arriving folded and opening into its words, twice.

Drafts survive everything in the evidence: the composer holds "the second one, then" and a reply chip across all six panels of 11_chat_scroll_strip.png and across 06_unfolding; reliability.json's draft_survival check says draft and pairing were intact after the client process was closed and reopened, and kill_mid_send says the host received it once with no duplicate on retry.

The clips are not padded. I measured mean absolute luma change between consecutive frames at quarter scale on all five: the longest run under 0.5 grey levels is 15 frames (240 ms of app time) in 08 and 07, 20 frames in 15, 5 frames in 06 and none at all in 11_chat_scroll — which agrees with frames.json's held_frame_test reporting repeated_frames 0 and longest_still_run 0 for every clip.

Ordering reads correctly wherever it can be read: the scroll strip advances Thu 23 Apr → Mon 27 Apr → Tue 28 Apr → Fri 1 May → Sat 2 May → Sun 3 May with no repeat, 11_chat_scroll.fling.json's scroll offset is monotonic 0 → 27570.7 with moved equal to asked on all 300 frames, and every report's cursor equals its events except the two cases named in the findings.

evidence/logs/tests.log ends "All tests passed!" at 287 passed, 1 skipped, including spine_test "append persists, replays in order, and the outbox comes back after reopen", floors_test "a message that did not go looks nothing like one that was read", a_refusal_says_why_test and the_thread_says_the_link_is_down_test.

10_first_run.png says the empty state honestly and in the right voice ("nothing from them yet. the six words are on the other phone.", "first one's yours. whatever it is it only goes to one person.") with events 0 in its report, and 17_setup_pwa.png walks the tailnet, the profile, the home screen, the six words and the interruption rules without a single exclamation mark.
verdict: This is a broadly complete messenger and one measured fault is holding the row under its floor. Text, photographs, video, voice notes, replies, edits, withdrawals, refusals that say why, typing, drafts that survive a process death, full-text and faceted search, a media library of 183 items with no empty tile, a media viewer with a playing film, and a link that goes down and comes back with a note that says "waiting to send" and then "sent ✓" — all of that is on the glass, in the couple's voice, with the capture's own reports agreeing with the pictures. The blocking finding is the scroll: evidence/logs/scroll_webkit.json says 196 of 886 frames of the dense throw cost over 400 ms of the app's own build time, p95 781 ms and max 1087 ms, with no 300-frame window anywhere in the record holding fewer than 64 of them and the longest clean run six frames; recomputed from per_frame, a frame that draws two paper pieces costs a median 654 ms against 3 ms for one that draws none, correlating 0.79 with pieces drawn and -0.12 with rows built, so this is the paper pipeline and not the container's missing GPU, which the file itself quarantines in raster_ms. The set carries its own control and makes it worse: the identical fling on the same instrument two days earlier, in both arms of evidence/experiments/what_the_alternates_cost, reads p95 34 ms with zero fling frames over 400 ms. 11_chat_scroll.mp4 cannot show any of this because its clock is driven at a fixed 16 ms a step, so the smooth clip and the fling log's perfect frame-for-frame travel are properties of the harness, not promises about a phone — and a thread that hitches for two-thirds of a second every fourth frame is the single thing in this evidence most likely to send either of them back to Instagram, because scrolling the year is the thing they will do most. Behind it sit five more serious findings: a 401 "the signature does not match" on the event long poll in three of fifteen scenes, no reaction legible in any artifact despite the set's own plan saying where one would be photographed, a reconnect whose landing is a single-frame cut and whose returning message never unfolds, a no-duplicates-and-monotonic claim taken entirely over zero-latency loopback with the tailnet leg eight days stale and its recheck pending, and a six-to-seven-second cold start with the year in it that no picture in the set shows.

not_worth_opening.why: the feeling vocabulary's waveforms and the derivation of its felt_distance floor. No message is delivered or lost by them, and the asked_a_motor_for lists that bear on whether a phone was asked for anything are carried in the region reports, which I did read.

measurements of the paper, the tear profile, the contact shadow, the rules on the stock and the typefaces. These are the material-truth row's; the one I opened, flat.json, I opened only because a blank sheet in a clip made me want to know whether the set had a paper-fallback fill anywhere, and it says it does not.

the reception scene's own step log. I read reception.json, reception.report.json and reception_picked_up.report.json, which carry what the push path actually did and what the browser was holding afterwards; the step trace adds nothing about message delivery that those three do not already say.

the framing for scenes outside the thread. I read every scene script for the six messenger artifacts (02, 06, 08, 11, 12, 13, 14) because telling a fault in the app from a fault in the framing needs them; for the pulse, us, moments, settings, feeling and setup scenes the region reports carry the sync and link state I needed and the framing is not in question.

the second arm's scene and report records. The two arms differ only by a font flag and what_the_alternates_cost.json plus both scroll_webkit_*.json files carry the comparison I needed; I opened the alternates arm's report and fling to confirm the fling was the same throw (travelled 27645, rows_built_total 170).

MANIFEST.json and WHY_MISSING.json point at it for why 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png are absent, but it is outside evidence/ and so outside what a critic is given. I have taken the reason as far as the evidence carries it and said in a finding that the rest of it is not checkable from here.
another reader's conclusions, closed as instructed.
